questions.prompt: What is the cause of “physiological shunt” occurrence?
options: Decreasing the cardiac output to half
Decreasing of ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
Mixing of pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
Increasing of VA/Q ratio more than normal amount
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Zero V/Q produces shunt, but bronchial venous admixture also contributes to physiological shunt. The broad wording therefore permits two mechanisms; the source-selected low-V/Q answer is retained only as provenance.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 1; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which zone(s) is (are) seen in a healthy subject during exercise?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the simplified West-zone model, exercise raises pulmonary vascular pressures and recruits upper-lung vessels toward continuous zone-III flow; this is a teaching model, not a universal all-intensities boundary.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 2; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is TRUE about “the duration of expiration”?
options: Increases by strong activation of pneumotaxic center
Is less than duration of inspiration during normal and quite respiration
Is affected by ventral respiratory group (VRG) during normal respiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A faster respiratory cycle generally shortens expiration. Quiet expiration is usually longer than inspiration and mainly passive; stronger pontine switch-off shortens rather than prolongs the cycle.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 3; source page 1.

questions.prompt: In which one the following, the diffusion rate of gases is decreased between two sides of respiratory membrane?
options: Increasing the gas pressure difference between the two sides of the membrane
Removal of part of the lungs
Decreasing the thickness of the membrane
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Removing lung reduces exchange area and therefore decreases diffusion rate when the gas and pressure gradient are unchanged.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 4; source page 1.

questions.prompt: In the lungs, which one of the following is NOT a barrier to gas exchange between capillary and the alveolar space?
options: A fluid layer of water and surfactants covering the luminal surface of alveolar cells
Smooth muscle cells surrounding the endothelial cells
Basement membranes of endothelial and alveolar cells
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The thin exchange barrier contains epithelium, interstitium/basement membranes and endothelium, not a continuous surrounding smooth-muscle layer.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 5; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is TRUE about bronchial circulation?
options: Supplies blood flow to conducting zone
Provides pulmonary capillary perfusion for gas exchange
Has vasoconstriction in response to hypoxia
Is a part of the the low-pressure circulation
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Bronchial systemic arteries nourish conducting airways. Pulmonary arteries provide the low-pressure alveolar capillary circulation.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 6; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lung volume or capacity is more than the others?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional adult reference volumes place inspiratory reserve volume above functional residual capacity, residual volume and expiratory reserve volume; actual values vary with body size and physiology.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 7; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the the initial pressure difference (mmHg) that causes O2 to diffuse into the pulmonary capillary?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The initial O2 gradient is approximately 104 mmHg in alveolar gas minus 40 mmHg in entering mixed venous blood: 64 mmHg. This is not the smaller mean gradient along the capillary.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 8; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of an increase in the CO2 of blood?
options: Decreases the affinity of oxyhemoglobin for oxygen
Decreases dissociation of O2 from oxyhemoglobin
Shifts the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the left
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased CO2 reduces hemoglobin's oxygen affinity and promotes unloading through the Bohr effect, shifting the curve right.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 9; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following center is thought to control of the respiratory rate?
options: Ventral respiratory group of medullary neurons
Dorsal respiratory group of medullary neurons
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the traditional exam model, the pneumotaxic region limits inspiratory duration and thereby influences respiratory rate. Rhythm generation also requires medullary networks.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 10; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is “the maximum amount of air that can be expired after a maximum inspiration”?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vital capacity is the maximum expired volume after maximal inspiration: IRV + tidal volume + ERV.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 11; source page 3.

questions.prompt: If a patient had a progressive lung disease that required an ever increasing pressure to fill the same volume of lung, how would the lung's compliance be affected?
options: These variables do not affect lung compliance.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Compliance is change in volume divided by change in distending pressure. Needing more pressure for the same volume means lower compliance.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 12; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Given your knowledge regarding the response of the pulmonary vasculature to oxygen content, where is the highest amount of blood flow through a normally oxygenated lung in a normal weight adult male that is standing upright?
options: To the midzone of the lung
To the bottom of the lung
To the top of the lung
There is no gradient across the lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Gravity produces greater pulmonary perfusion at the base than the apex in the healthy upright lung.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 13; source page 3.

questions.prompt: In response to hypoxia, which neurotransmitter is NOT released by “Glomus cells” in the carotid bodies?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The supplied selection of histamine is not a reliable absolute exclusion: primary carotid-body research identifies histamine in glomus cells and supports a modulatory role. Transmitter release varies with species and conditions; no uniquely defensible NOT-released option is established.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 14; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the chloride shift in RBC of venous blood?
options: HCO3- goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
chloride ion goes out of the cell and H+ goes into the cell
chloride ion goes into the cell and HCO3- goes out of the cell
H+ goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: During systemic tissue CO2 uptake, bicarbonate formed inside erythrocytes exits in exchange for chloride entering. The exchanger reverses direction during pulmonary CO2 unloading.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 15; source page 3.

questions.prompt: If a patient's blood carries 10 grams of hemoglobin per deciliter, what is the maximum O2 carrying capacity of blood (milliliters per deciliter) in this person?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using 1.34 mL O2 per gram of fully saturated hemoglobin, 10 × 1.34 = 13.4 mL O2/dL, excluding the small dissolved component.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 16; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following gas has more “diffusing capacity” than others in resting?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2 has much greater solubility and an approximately twentyfold larger membrane diffusion coefficient than O2; its diffusing capacity exceeds the other listed gases in the teaching comparison.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 17; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following leads to shift to the left of O2 dissociation curve?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Lower H+ concentration means higher pH and a leftward shift with increased oxygen affinity; increased metabolism, CO2 or acidity favor a rightward shift.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 18; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following has afferent nerve fibers in the vagus nerve?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Aortic-body afferents travel in the vagus (X); carotid-body afferents travel through Hering's nerve to glossopharyngeal (IX).

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 19; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following list includes only structures that compose the anatomic dead-space?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Trachea, bronchi and terminal bronchioles are conducting airways and constitute anatomical dead space. Respiratory bronchioles and alveoli participate in exchange.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 20; source page 4.

questions.prompt: What is the minute respiratory volume (L/min); with a tidal volume of 0.8 L and respiratory rate of 15 breaths/min?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Minute ventilation = tidal volume × respiratory rate = 0.8 × 15 = 12 L/min; no dead-space subtraction is requested.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 21; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following occurs during normal inspiration?
options: Diaphragm contracts, pleural and alveolar pressures decrease
Diaphragm relaxes, external intercostals contract, pleural pressure increases
External and internal intercostals contract, pleural and alveolar pressure increase
Diaphragm contracts, pleural pressure increases, alveolar pressure decreases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Inspiratory diaphragm contraction expands the thorax, makes pleural pressure more negative and transiently lowers alveolar pressure below atmospheric pressure to draw air inward.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 22; source page 5.

questions.prompt: In which of the following is observed Stratified Squamous Tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Both the nasal vestibule and the oro-/laryngopharyngeal portions of the pharynx contain stratified squamous epithelium. The stem does not restrict the region, so the marked vestibule is not unique.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 23; source page 5.

questions.prompt: What Is The Name Cell Secreted Surfactant In Bronchios?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Celara is the source's spelling of Clara (club) cells, which secrete protective surfactant components in bronchioles. Bronchios is imprecise; this is the intended bronchiolar cell, distinct from alveolar type II cells.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 24; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is observed in structure Histology In Respiratory Zone?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Here Respiratory Zone denotes nasal respiratory mucosa, whose epithelium includes goblet cells. The distal gas-exchange zone would be a different meaning and normally lacks goblet cells.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 25; source page 5.

questions.prompt: In which of the following is observed Elastic Fiber In Histology Stractuer ?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Elastic fibers occur in the larynx and in distal lung structures including alveolar ducts; the broad location question has more than one defensible option.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 26; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which part of the lung tissue has Nomocyte II?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Nomocyte II is the source's misspelling of type II pneumocyte, an alveolar epithelial cell that produces surfactant.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 27; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which bone is involved in both the roof and the medial surface of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Ethmoid contributes the cribriform nasal roof and perpendicular plate of the septum. Palatine contributes floor/lateral-wall structures, not the requested roof-and-medial-wall combination; the supplied palatine mark is corrected.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 28; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which of the following muscles is involved in pulling thyroid cartilage downward and forward ؟
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid cartilage forward and downward relative to the cricoid, elongating and tensing the vocal ligaments.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 29; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the highest structure in the right lung umbilicus?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The right superior lobar (eparterial) bronchus lies above the right pulmonary artery and is the highest listed hilar structure; umbilicus here means hilum.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 30; source page 6.

questions.prompt: The medial surface of the right lung is adjacent to all the following structures except ....
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The aortic arch relates to the left lung; the right mediastinal surface relates to the venae cavae and azygos system.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 31; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which of the following paranasal sinuses open to the apex of bulla ethmoidal ؟
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Middle ethmoidal air cells open on the ethmoidal bulla in the middle meatus.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 32; source page 7.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the upper and free side of the quadrangular membrane?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The superior free edge of the quadrangular membrane forms the aryepiglottic fold; its inferior edge forms the vestibular ligament.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 33; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which of the following nerve pass through incisive canal ?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The nasopalatine nerve passes through the incisive canal to the anterior hard palate.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 34; source page 7.

questions.prompt: All of the following bones participates in the formation of the lateral wall of the nose except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vomer forms the inferior/posterior nasal septum rather than the lateral nasal wall.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 35; source page 7.

questions.prompt: All of the following structures are seen in inlet of larynx except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vestibular fold lies within the laryngeal cavity, below the inlet. The epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds and posterior arytenoid region bound the inlet.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 36; source page 8.

questions.prompt: Which of the following arteries passes through the foramen in roof of nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The anterior ethmoidal artery reaches the nasal cavity through the roof near the cribriform plate; the sphenopalatine artery enters through the lateral sphenopalatine foramen.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 37; source page 8.

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles are paralyzed by cutting the recurrent laryngeal nerve except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Cricothyroid is supplied by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; the listed other intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 38; source page 8.

questions.prompt: In which period of lungs development alveolar duct appear
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: In the canalicular period, respiratory bronchioles develop and branch into alveolar ducts; pseudoglandular development reaches terminal bronchioles only.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 9 February 2021; printed question 39; source page 8.

questions.prompt: In which time of development the second epithelial alveolar cells appear?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The course's Langman/E2 timing places type II-cell appearance near the end of the sixth month (about 24 weeks in the book), before full surfactant maturity.
